paragraphs.zh: In certain embodiments, there is provided a process for preparation of mesotrione of formula (I), which includes the steps of:
paragraphs.en: In certain embodiments, there is provided a process for preparation of mesotrione of formula (I), which includes the steps of:
paragraphs.notes: Document is in English, so zh and en are the identical printed string (brief section 1). The marker is printed as four digits on this page and is transcribed exactly, not padded and not trimmed. The paragraph introduces a three item list; the three items follow as separate entries below because each is separated from the next by a reaction scheme and by a printed line break, and rule 3 forbids an interior blank line.

paragraphs.zh: (i) oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) with an oxidant in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide as a catalyst, to produce 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III);
paragraphs.en: (i) oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) with an oxidant in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide as a catalyst, to produce 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III);
paragraphs.notes: Item (i) of paragraph [0039]; it carries no marker of its own, so marker is null rather than a guessed number. A later pass should join it to [0039]. Two printing features, both kept verbatim: the same moiety is spelled two ways one line apart, 'methylsulfonyl' with an f in the NMST name and 'methylsulphonyl' with a ph in the NMSBA name (brief section 8), and the text reads 'in presence of' with no 'the'. Both were confirmed at 6x. The left margin prints the line number 5 beside this line; margin line numbers are furniture and are excluded (brief section 5).

paragraphs.zh: (ii) reaction of NMSBA of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione to produce enol ester of formula (II); and
paragraphs.en: (ii) reaction of NMSBA of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione to produce enol ester of formula (II); and
paragraphs.notes: Item (ii) of paragraph [0039]; no marker of its own, so marker is null. The printed sentence is broken by the second reaction scheme: 'to produce enol' ends the line above the scheme, the words 'ester of' are printed to the right of the scheme's 'Formula II' label on the same row as the formula labels, and 'formula (II); and' is the next full line. It is recorded here as one continuous string in printed reading order, with no interior line break.

paragraphs.zh: (iii) conversion of the enol ester of formula (II) to mesotrione of formula (I)
paragraphs.en: (iii) conversion of the enol ester of formula (II) to mesotrione of formula (I)
paragraphs.notes: Item (iii) of paragraph [0039]; no marker of its own, so marker is null. Printed with no terminating punctuation, which is kept as printed. The left margin prints the line number 10 beside this line and it is excluded as furniture.

drawings.notes: Scheme for step (i) of the [0039] embodiment. It sits between the '(i) oxidation of ...' item line and the '(ii) reaction of NMSBA ...' item line, both of which belong to [0039], so the bracketing markers are [0039] and [0040]. The only text on the arrow is 'Oxidant / RuO2', printed ABOVE it; nothing at all is printed below the arrow. Ring positions were read off the drawn hexagons, not inferred: both rings are drawn vertex-up, the top vertex carries CH3 (left) or the COOH carbon (right), the upper-right vertex carries NO2, and the bottom vertex, para to the top one, carries the SO2 whose H3C is written to its lower left. The roman numerals in the two labels were checked at 6x because the degraded ink makes III and IV easy to confuse. This scheme appears to be the same artwork as the scheme on p15. Every bond and label in this scheme is rendered as broken dotted ink by the bitonal scan (brief section 9, the publication lost its greyscale). At 6x magnification no bond or ring position was left ambiguous. The reaction arrow looks dashed on the page but is a degraded solid line with one solid arrowhead, so it is recorded as solid.

drawings.notes: Scheme for step (ii) of the [0039] embodiment, printed inside the '(ii) reaction of NMSBA ...' sentence: the sentence breaks after 'to produce enol', the scheme follows, and the words 'ester of' are printed to the RIGHT of the 'Formula II' label on the same baseline row as the two formula labels, with 'formula (II); and' on the next full line. The arrow carries NOTHING above it and NOTHING below it: no reagent, no solvent, no catalyst, no temperature, no time. The 1,3-cyclohexanedione is the only structure on this page with no formula label under it. Its two C=O are on the top vertex and on the lower-left vertex of a vertex-up hexagon, which is a 1,3 relationship as read off the drawing. On the product, the ester oxygen is drawn onto the sp2 carbon of a ring C=C whose other end is the CH adjacent to the ring ketone, so the enol ester is the 3-oxocyclohex-1-en-1-yl ester as drawn, not the 1,3-dione tautomer. Every bond and label in this scheme is rendered as broken dotted ink by the bitonal scan (brief section 9, the publication lost its greyscale). At 6x magnification no bond or ring position was left ambiguous. The reaction arrow looks dashed on the page but is a degraded solid line with one solid arrowhead, so it is recorded as solid.

drawings.notes: Scheme for step (iii) of the [0039] embodiment, printed under the '(iii) conversion of the enol ester ...' line and above [0040]. The arrow carries NOTHING above it and NOTHING below it, so the rearrangement is drawn with no reagent, base, solvent or condition of any kind. On the product ring the two carbonyls are drawn as ketones, one on the top vertex and one on the lower-left vertex, with the benzoyl on the ring carbon between them and no ring C=C anywhere, so the keto form of the 1,3-dione is what is drawn, not an enol. That was checked at 7x specifically because the enol form is the other plausible reading. Every bond and label in this scheme is rendered as broken dotted ink by the bitonal scan (brief section 9, the publication lost its greyscale). At 6x magnification no bond or ring position was left ambiguous. The reaction arrow looks dashed on the page but is a degraded solid line with one solid arrowhead, so it is recorded as solid.

discrepancies.what: Within one sentence of [0039] item (i) the methylsulfonyl moiety is spelled two ways, while the two drawings beside it draw one and the same group.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Formula IV and Formula III both draw an identical H3C-SO2 group on ring carbon C4; the drawings give no basis for two different moieties.
discrepancies.text_says: Item (i) prints '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST)' with an f and, two lines later, '2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA)' with a ph. Both spellings are transcribed as printed and neither has been normalised.

discrepancies.what: Steps (ii) and (iii) are drawn with completely bare arrows, and the prose for those two steps names no reagent or condition either, so the page as a whole specifies no way to carry either step out.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The arrow in the step (ii) scheme and the arrow in the step (iii) scheme each carry nothing above and nothing below. Only the step (i) arrow is labelled, with 'Oxidant / RuO2'.
discrepancies.text_says: Item (ii) says only 'reaction of NMSBA of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione to produce enol ester of formula (II)' and item (iii) says only 'conversion of the enol ester of formula (II) to mesotrione of formula (I)'. Neither names a reagent, solvent, base, catalyst, temperature or time.
